messages:
Maya: FYI — AcmeRetail reported p99 tail spikes on dedicated pool last night, customer flagged potential SLA breach. Observed window 23:00-02:00 UTC, QPS ~25% above baseline. Anyone taking ownership for a short-term mitigation?

Liam: Can you paste the grafana panel and any engine logs? Is this model-related or routing/backpressure?

Maya: Panel: https://grafana.redwood/acme/p99. Logs show lots of 503s with 'queue full' coming from pool-gpu-12 around 23:10-23:40.

Sophia: If it's queueing we can enable burst_pool for that customer and route overflow to hosted small-variant. That would buy ~30m while we stabilize. I can flip the policy but need an owner to monitor during the window.

DevOpsBot: Alert: AcmeRetail dedicated-pool-12 high-queue at 2026-03-17T23:14:08Z — p99 latency 1.8s, queue depth 85.

Devon: I'll own the routing change. Plan: enable burst for AcmeRetail and set route fallback to hosted-medium-quant. Canary to 5% by 23:45 UTC, monitor for 15m, then ramp. @Arjun — need CR review for autoscaler tune so we don't under-react to the spike.

Arjun: On it — PR opened: https://git.redwood/infra/PR-790 (autoscaler: reduce cool_down from 300s to 90s for dedicated pools). Left a couple inline comments, should be able to review in ~20m.

Liam: Also double-check capacity reservations — if other customers share the same machines, burst could cause noisy neighbor issues.

Sophia: Good call. I'll reserve 1 GPU in pool-gpu-12 for the 23:00-02:00 UTC window and annotate the pool. Will update routing policy after Devon flips it.

Devon: Doing canary now. Steps: 1) apply policy patch 2) route 5% traffic to fallback 3) monitor p50/p95/p99 + error rate. Posting short logs as I go. :thumbsup:

Maya: Please also coordinate a short message to CS so they can notify the customer we're actively mitigating and will follow up with RCA.

Arjun: CR reviewed and updated, ready to merge after one small nits fix. If merged I'll promote the autoscaler change to canary in prod.

DevOpsBot: Deploybot: rollout started for routing-policy-canary by Devon at 2026-03-17T23:32:10Z.

Devon: Canary metrics look promising — canary slice p99 down from 1.8s -> 0.85s. No error increase. Ramping to 25% now.

Maya: Great work. Once at 100% please drop a final status here and confirm CS notified. We'll collect follow-up actions (postmortem, longer-term autoscaler tuning, capacity reservations) after stabilization.

Devon: Ramp at 100% completed at 2026-03-17T23:58Z. p99 stabilised ~0.9s. Changed routing policy and left rollback flag in case of regressions.

Arjun: Autoscaler tweak promoted to prod canary; monitoring for unexpected oscillation.

Sophia: I'll file a short runbook entry in the infra wiki for 'dedicated pool weekend spikes' and schedule a sync with capacity planning.

Maya: Thanks everyone. Will ping #customer-success to confirm the customer message and link this thread to the incident notes.
